summary: binding.gyp triggers execution of a Caesar-cipher + AES-GCM obfuscated loader on npm install
details: The package ships a binding.gyp whose sources field uses GYP command expansion `<!(env node index.js...; echo stub.c)` to shell out and run `node index.js` during node-gyp rebuild. The gyp target type is `none` and no C/C++ sources are shipped, so the file has no legitimate native-build purpose; its only effect is to invoke index.js at install time. index.js is a ~586KB char-code array decoded via a Caesar-shift substitution and passed to eval. The decoded body uses node:crypto createDecipheriv("aes-128-gcm") with hardcoded hex key/IV/AAD to decrypt a large hex ciphertext, wrapped in a self-executing async IIFE with a swallowed catch. The combination of a build-config command-expansion execution vector, absence of any real native source, and a multi-layer obfuscated/encrypted opaque payload executed at install is the canonical install-time dropper shape — the installer runs attacker-supplied code on `npm install` with no visibility into what the decrypted payload does.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
